sentences.text:
=
 The State Of Bihar and Ors
 ... ... Appe
 Versus
 Shafta Jubi and Ors.
 ... ... Respondent/s
 ======================================================
 Appearance :

For the Appellant/s : Mr. K.P. Gupta, Gp-10 with
 Mr. Virendra Kuar, Ac to Gp-10

For the Respondent/s : Mr. Patanjali Rishi, Adv.
 ========

==============================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE KHATIM REZA  CAV ORDER 16 08-10-2024 Re: I.A. No. 4238 of 2016 This interlocutory application has been filed for condoning the delay in filing the instant Second Appeal.
2. Learned counsel for the appellants has submitted that on 20.04.2015, the judgment and decree under appeal has been passed.

The appellant applied for requisition of certified copy of judgment and decree dated 20.04.2015 on 28.04.2015, the same was notified on 14.05.2015 and stamp was supplied on 16.05.2015 and certified copy of judgment and decree was supplied on 26.05.2015.
After receiving of the certified copy of judgment and decree under appeal, legal opinion was sought from Government Pleader on 26.06.2015.
The Educational Training Institute wrote a letter to the Collector, Banka for its opinion.
The opinion was given by the Government Pleader on Patna High Court SA No.213 of 2016(16) dt.08-10-2024 27.08.2015 to the Collector, Banka for filing the appeal.

The said opinion was also sent to the Director Research and Training Education Department,
Government of Bihar on 29.09.2015.

The District Education and Training Institute (DIET), Banka wrote to Director Education Training Bihar on 23.11.2015 and sought permission for filing appeal against the judgment and decree under appeal.
The opinion was given by the Director Education and Training Patna, Government of Bihar on 03.03.2016 for filing the instant appeal.

The Law Department Government of Bihar gave permission to file Second appeal on 12.04.2016 and on 13.04.2016, concerned file was sent to the office of learned Advocate General, Bihar for opinion and The State Of Bihar And Ors vs Shafta Jubi And Ors.

1 filing the appeal.
Soon thereafter, the instant appeal was filed on 12.05.2016.
On notice, respondent nos. 1 to 6 appeared but no counter affidavit was filed in limitation matter.
3. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances made in the interlocutory application, it shows that cause of delay has been sufficiently and properly explained.
4. Considering the aforesaid explanation, the delay in filing of the instant Second Appeal is condoned.
5. Accordingly, I.A. No. 4238 of 2016 is allowed.
Re: I.A. No. 7396 of 2018 Patna High Court SA No.213 of 2016(16) dt.08-10-2024 6.

This interlocutory application has been filed for accepting the notices upon respondent nos. 3, 4,
and 6 which were received by respondent no 5.
Hence, this jointness petition has been filed.

7. It appears from the record that respondent nos. 1 to 6 have appeared through their counsel and a duly executed Vakalatnama on behalf of the aforesaid respondents has been filed, which is on record.
8. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances, the interlocutory application becomes infructuous as the respondents have appeared and filed duly executed Vakalatnama through their counsel.
9. Accordingly, I.A. No. 7396 of 2018 is disposed of as infructuous.
10. Heard learned counsel for the appellants and learned counsel for the respondents.

11. Admit.
12.
Call for the lower court records.

13. This Second Appeal shall be considered on the following substantial questions of law:-
(i) Whether the land in suit (Schedule-C) was acquired for the expansion of Junior Training School at Banka Patna High Court SA No.213 of 2016(16) dt.08-10-2024 by the Government of Bihar in exercise of the power conferred by Section 17(4) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1984 by notification dated 21.11.1956.
(ii).
Whether vendor/mother, namely, Bibi Sarifan of the original plaintiffs had received the compensation amount on 13.04.1957 with regard to Schedule-C property?
(iii). Whether Plot Nos. 355, 189, 356 and 354 situated in village-Karharia measuring an area 1 Acre 81 decimals is acquired by notification dated 21.11.1956?

The State Of Bihar And Ors vs Shafta Jubi And Ors. on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37669779/
2 (iv).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Whether the suit is barred by law of limitation?
(v). Whether the learned Appellate Court exceeded its jurisdiction and granted relief which was not claimed by the plaintiffs/respondents?
14. Learned counsel for the respondent nos. 1 to 6 accepts the appeal notice on behalf of them.

This interlocutory application has been filed for stay of further proceeding of Execution Case No.
02 of 2022 pending in the Court of Sub-Judge-VI, Banka till disposal of the Second Appeal.

16. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that plaintiffs/respondents filed Title Suit No. 94 of 1985 for Patna High Court SA No.213 of 2016(16) dt.08-10-2024 declaration of right, title and interest over the suit land (Schedule-C) and also declared that entry in Municipal Survey Khatiyan of Ward Nos. 7 and 8 published on 10.02.1985 in favour of defendant no. 2 with respect to the suit land is quite illegal, fraudulent, collusive, wrong, null and void and also not binding upon the plaintiffs.
The suit land and other land was acquired by the State of Bihar for the purpose of expansion of Junior Basic Training School at Banka in the year 1956.
Since then the appellants are in possession of the suit land.
The suit land is in possession of the institution and appellants are imparting education to children since 1958.
17. Learned counsel submits that the present suit was filed after 29 years of acquisition of the aforesaid land.
The survey authority rightly recorded the name of the appellants.
Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that if the execution case is not stayed, the appellants shall suffer irreparable loss.
18. On the other hand learned counsel for the respondents vehemently opposed the prayer of the appellants.
19. Learned counsel for the plaintiffs/respondents submits that if the execution case is stayed, the plaintiffs are restrained from using the usufruct of the decree.
Both the courts
Patna High Court SA No.213 of 2016(16) dt.08-10-2024 have concurrently passed the decree in favour of the plaintiffs/respondents.

20. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and averments made in the interlocutory application, the further proceeding of Execution Case No. 02 of 2022 shall remain stayed pending in the court of Sub-Judge-I, Banka till further order.

(Khatim Reza, J) prabhat/-
U The State Of Bihar And Ors vs Shafta Jubi And Ors.
